speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the rear-end collision and the subsequent right groin pain with abnormal leg positioning. To begin my assessment, can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned immediately after the accident, and do you recall hearing or feeling a "pop" at the time?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you describe the specific abnormal position your right leg is currently in, and are you able to move your hip or knee voluntarily? Additionally, have you noticed any significant shortening or rotation of the right leg compared to the left?

REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The right leg is positioned in a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated posture compared to the left. Voluntary movement of the right hip and knee is limited due to pain and the abnormal positioning. Significant shortening and internal rotation of the right leg are present. Pelvic_X-ray findings indicate no fractures in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests a posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Traumatic Right Hip Posterior Dislocation.

Based on the classic shortening, adduction, and internal rotation of the leg combined with the X-ray findings of posterior dislocation and no pelvic fracture, this confirms your diagnosis. We will need urgent orthopedic consultation for closed reduction to prevent avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
